tickets.title: Litter and missing corner trash baskets near Franklin
tickets.summary: A resident who gathered about 30 neighbors in their building reported that litter and broken glass are the top local complaint, especially on Franklin with heavy foot traffic from school and college students. The speaker said there are no corner baskets nearby, so people throw trash on the ground, and suggested signs asking neighbors to keep the area clean. Residents in the building are willing to join a weekly Saturday morning litter cleanup. Action: Ask DSNY to add more corner litter baskets near Franklin and to support a community litter cleanup day.

tickets.title: Clogged sewer grates and flooding near homes
tickets.summary: A resident says a sewer grate at a nearby corner fills with garbage and leaves and causes flooding, and that DEP clears it only after a call. The resident keeps the grate clean and wants a QR code reporting tool like the existing one, so neighbors can report clogged sewer grates. The resident notes that DEP has a new bureau and that the resident plans to bring its commissioner in for a meeting, which implies an earlier DEP meeting. Action: Ask DEP to set up a QR code reporting option for clogged sewer grates and to follow up with the resident on the planned meeting with the new bureau commissioner.

tickets.title: People entering sewers through manholes
tickets.summary: Residents reported a police report of people entering the sewers through a manhole, which alarmed neighbors and was described as a recurring problem. Police responded to the call but found nothing, and they arrested a man waiting outside on an outstanding warrant. The residents want to know how the people get in and what they are doing there. Action: Ask DEP and NYPD for an explanation of the sewer entries and for measures to secure the manholes.

tickets.title: Street sweeping frequency and enforcement in Crown Heights
tickets.summary: A Crown Heights Community Council representative said a council member's street sweeping pilot ended, and that streets in this district still get cleaned only once a week for many months, while other areas get two days. The speaker said parked cars are not moved and enforcement is weak, and that the sweepers appear to focus on GPS data rather than actually cleaning. The speaker urged residents to file 311 complaints together to push DSNY to respond. Action: Ask DSNY to restore twice-weekly street sweeping in the district, enforce parking rules, and report the pilot results.

tickets.title: Textile and e-waste bins for a large building
tickets.summary: A resident of a 300-unit building reported that DSNY has pushed back on building compost bins, and that the resident has not yet followed up on textile collection bins. The resident is also interested in e-waste collection, which DSNY provides through vendors for large buildings. The resident said the building did not get a reply from DSNY on the textile bins. Action: Ask the district office to help the building follow up with DSNY on textile bins, e-waste collection, and the compost bins.
